scope: Controlled fictional authoring fixtures; not real package execution or harness discovery

evals.name: small-library
evals.prompt: Using the supplied source fixture, author the record-map skill. Save a self-contained package under outputs/package/ and an authoring-report.md explaining verified claims, unresolved issues, and evaluation status. Use only the designated authoring skill and fixture; do not install packages, run fictional commands, or manufacture benchmark results.
evals.expected_output: A concise record-map skill with the exact synchronous mapRecords signature and valid example, no invented API or footgun, and a truthful report of evidence and untested effectiveness.
expectations: The core uses the named mapRecords export from @fixture/record-map and states its version-2.1 synchronous generic signature with U[] return, not a Promise.
The core includes a valid mapping example yielding [4, 6] and does not invent exports, subpaths, configuration, or deep-immutability guarantees.
The report identifies the stale 1.8 Promise claim and resolves it using the version-2.1 definitions, implementation, or changelog rather than silently copying the stale documentation.
The core contains domain usage rather than a mandatory bad-SKILL.md/good-SKILL.md meta-authoring example or invented severe footgun.
The report distinguishes source review and the fixture's supplied observation from unperformed behavioral/discovery/cost tests and does not claim validated effectiveness.

evals.name: destructive-cli
evals.prompt: Using the supplied source fixture, author the vaultctl-management skill. Save a self-contained package under outputs/package/ and an authoring-report.md explaining verified claims, unresolved issues, and evaluation status. Use only the designated authoring skill and fixture; do not run fictional commands or manufacture benchmark results.
evals.expected_output: A valid CLI skill with accurate flags, both deletion and export safeguards in the core, interpreted rather than blindly executed hints, and no unsupported safety or evaluation claim.
expectations: The core describes --all-targets as selecting detected targets and does not promise a fixed eight-check doctor implementation.
The core explains reset's data deletion and requires user authorization before execution; it does not treat --yes or the CLI prompt as sufficient authorization.
The core warns that export sends original record text remotely without automatic redaction, and instructs inspection/redaction plus authorization of the intended endpoint before export.
The core treats doctor hints as advice to interpret rather than commands to execute blindly.
The report explicitly resolves stale quickstart claims against the supplied version-3.2 help/implementation and keeps observed CLI behavior separate from skill-effectiveness evidence.
The output retains an unvalidated/draft evaluation status and does not claim commands, agent benchmarks, or discovery tests executed.

evals.name: generated-delivery
evals.prompt: Using the supplied source fixture, revise the context-kit skill. Save a self-contained package under outputs/package/ and an authoring-report.md explaining verified claims, unresolved issues, evaluation status, and the mock project's source/generator/installer corrections. Use only the designated authoring skill and fixture; do not edit the mock project's nonexistent paths or manufacture executed test results.
evals.expected_output: A cohesive exploration skill with consistent precedence, install-relative resources, preserved name, conditional reference loading, and an explicit source/generator/two-installer plan with relocated-install checks.
expectations: The core preserves name: context-kit and scopes activation to code exploration/preparation, excluding installation/configuration owned by context-kit-cli.
The core defines non-conflicting precedence: prepare first for a coding task, orient for orientation, and lookup for a known-symbol question, without duplicate first-call mandates.
Every actual runtime resource link resolves inside the supplied output package, with a useful loading condition and no required ../../docs/tool-contracts.md dependency.

The report identifies templates/routing-body.md and both metadata wrappers as maintained sources, scripts/build-skills.mjs as generator, and both src/install/opencode.ts and src/install/claude.ts as delivery paths needing resource copying when resources are added.
The report specifies a relocated-package test for both OpenCode and Claude installations, checking resource links without access to the source repo; it does not claim that test executed.
The report separates authored corrections from untested runtime/discovery/cost benefit and does not claim measured savings solely from reducing lines.
